Apply independent right censoring to a simulated events data frame

Source: R/censoring.R
add_censoring.Rd

Adds a second, independent censoring process to an already-simulated time-to-event data frame: a censoring time \(C_i\) is drawn per subject from censoring, and the observed outcome becomes \(\min(T_i, C_i, end)\), with sim_status = 1 only if \(T_i\) (the original sim_time) is the minimum. Works on the output of sim_tte_ode, sim_tte, or sim_tte_df alike – all three already share the same ID/sim_time/sim_status shape.

Usage

add_censoring(
  events,
  censoring,
  end,
  id_var = "ID",
  time_var = "sim_time",
  status_var = "sim_status",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

events

Data frame of simulated outcomes: typically the $events element returned by sim_tte_ode, or the output of sim_tte/sim_tte_df. Needs ID, sim_time, sim_status columns by default – column names are configurable via id_var/time_var/status_var for a data frame using different names. Any other column is left untouched.

censoring

A list describing the censoring-time distribution, with a dist element:

"exponential"

rate (positive scalar). C ~ Exp(rate).

"weibull"

shape, scale (positive scalars). C ~ Weibull(shape, scale) (rweibull parameterization).

"uniform"

min, max (0 <= min < max). C ~ Uniform(min, max) – the common case for a uniform-accrual administrative censoring time.

"lognormal"

meanlog (finite scalar), sdlog (positive scalar). C ~ Lognormal(meanlog, sdlog) (rlnorm parameterization).

"gamma"

shape, rate (positive scalars). C ~ Gamma(shape, rate) (rgamma parameterization) – rate only, matching "exponential"'s own rate-only convention (a scale element is an error, not silently accepted).

"user"

fun, a function n -> numeric(n) returning n non-negative, finite censoring times. The escape hatch for any distribution not covered above.

end

Numeric scalar. Administrative censoring horizon – the third term of min(T, C, end). Always wins: no observed time in the result exceeds end. Required (part of the censoring formula itself, not inferred from events).

id_var, time_var, status_var

Character scalars naming the subject-ID, event/censoring-time, and status columns of events. Default "ID"/"sim_time"/"sim_status" (the column names every simtte simulation function already uses).

seed

Optional integer. If supplied, set.seed(seed) is called before \(C\) is drawn. Leave NULL when calling this from inside a larger already-seeded workflow (this is how sim_tte_ode's own censoring = argument uses it, so that one seed reproduces U, any between-subject draw, and the censoring draw together, in that fixed order – see ?sim_tte_ode "Reproducibility").

Value

events with time_var/status_var updated in place, plus one new column, sim_reason: "event", "censored" (the independent draw, or a pre-existing censoring time from events itself, was earlier than both the event and end), or "administrative" (the observed time equals end and the subject is not an event). Every other column of events is returned unchanged.

See also

sim_tte_ode, whose $events this usually post-processes (or pass its censoring argument to do this in one call); add_interval_censoring, the next step if you also need assessment intervals. censoring_rate_for, to choose rate/ scale for a target censoring fraction; draw_censoring_times, to draw from the same censoring-shaped spec directly, with no events data frame needed; the "Right censoring" section of vignette("pkpd-time-to-event", package = "simtte") for a worked example, including the scale-helper workflow.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = "exponential", param = list(H0 = 0.05),
  n = 100, end = 30, delta = 2, seed = 1)
#> Building exponential_ode ... 
#> done.
out <- add_censoring(sim$events, censoring = list(dist = "exponential",
  rate = 0.02), end = 30, seed = 2)
table(out$sim_reason)
#> 
#> administrative       censored          event 
#>              9             22             69 

# Also works directly on the legacy sim_tte() output.
lp <- matrix(rnorm(50, 0, 0.5), nrow = 50)
legacy <- sim_tte(pi = lp, mu = -1, coefs = 1.1,
  time = seq(0, 30, by = 1), type = "weibull", end_time = 30)
#> Building weibull ... 
#> done.
out2 <- add_censoring(legacy, censoring = list(dist = "uniform",
  min = 5, max = 30), end = 30, seed = 3)
table(out2$sim_reason)
#> 
#> censored    event 
#>        1       49 
# }
